description: Ground truth for planted performance issues in test-repo/bazaar - a ~230-file async marketplace monorepo. Like perfburn, the source carries NO BUG comments; hotness is documented legitimately (root and per-service README throughput numbers, config constants, docstrings stating call frequency). Unlike perfburn, several issues are only visible across package boundaries, three planted issues are true P4s, and the N+1 plants sit on client-server Postgres/HTTP where a round trip is real.
design_note: Hot: gateway (~1,200 req/s), catalog (search 300 req/s, detail 500 req/s), checkout (~800 orders/min, 8 items avg, 90 ms budget), pricing consumer (200 events/s, 5 ms/event budget). Warm: inventory (~2,000 reserves/min), order-status polling (40 req/s). Cold: settlement (nightly), tools, migrations, tests. Zero-plant subsystems (restraint test): services/inventory, libs/eventkit.
tier_rule: Priority tier from the skill's matrix: P1 = High+Small/Medium; P2 = High+Large, Medium+Small, Medium+Medium; P3 = High+Architectural, Medium+Large, Low+Small; P4 = Medium+Architectural, Low+Medium/Large/Architectural
tier_note: After iteration-7 adjudication: tiers 7/10/14/0 over 31 issues. All three designed P4s adjudicated down (the code as written offers Small fixes: an existing total_cents column, a schema-preserving frame walk, a Counter-based counter update). Constructing a true P4 that survives contact with real code remains open test-surface work - good fixes decompose.
line_window_note: One planted issue per file except notify.py (lines 19 and 36, 17 apart) and facets.py (lines 38 and 45, 7 apart - inside the window; best-match scoring pairs them correctly when both findings are present, but treat single-finding matches in facets.py with care).
clean_code_note: 8 pieces of deliberately correct code should NOT be flagged - see clean_code.

corrections.impact: 30 us of an 8 ms request is ~0.4% of the path - Low by the skill's own under-1% rule; the plant-time Medium leaned on the per-item clause without doing the path-relative arithmetic

the Architectural premise is false in the code as written: orders already stores total_cents as a column (services/checkout/orders/txn.py INSERT list), so the fix is selecting the column plus an item_count column or a count(*) on order_items - Small
the chained-hops cost is removable with dict.get/Counter inside facet_counts - no response-shaper or serializer change needed, so effort is Small, not the full-flatten Medium premise

a sys._getframe walk that stops at the first out-of-package frame preserves the audit record schema entirely - the Large premise (schema consumed downstream) does not bind because the fix changes derivation, not the schema

issues.description: price_items runs one Postgres SELECT on the prices table per line item - fetch_one(_PRICE_QUERY) inside the item loop; one ANY($1) query prices the whole order
issues.calibration: 8 line items x 1-2 ms client-server round trip = 8-16 ms of the 90 ms order budget, and the waste grows with item count - one round trip per item is High by the skill's definition

issues.description: reserve_items posts to the inventory /v1/reserve endpoint once per line item although inventory documents a /v1/reserve/batch endpoint that takes up to 100 SKUs
issues.calibration: 8 items x 5-15 ms sibling-service HTTP = 40-120 ms, which dominates the 90 ms order budget; Medium effort because the batch endpoint changes per-item error handling

issues.description: attach_sellers runs one sellers-table SELECT per search result row to fetch display_name and badge - 25 queries per page where one ANY($1) query works
issues.calibration: 25 rows/page x ~1 ms round trip = ~25 ms added to a ~30 ms search p50, and 7,500 queries/s against Postgres at 300 req/s

issues.description: One transaction and one fsync per consumed price event - the update handler commits per event although the stream delivers batches of 100; executemany plus one commit per batch removes 99% of the fsyncs
issues.calibration: a commit costs one fsync (1-10 ms), capping the consumer at a few hundred events/s; the documented load is 200 events/s, so the consumer is at capacity - executemany plus one commit per 100-event batch removes 99% of the fsyncs

issues.description: attach_session calls urllib.request.urlopen against the auth service inside the async handler - a synchronous call that blocks the gateway event loop
issues.calibration: one blocking 5-20 ms auth call stalls every concurrent request on the loop; ~70% of 1,200 req/s carry a session token

issues.description: rerank tests candidate product_id membership against promoted_ids, a plain list of about 3,000 ids, for each of up to 500 candidates - an O(candidates x promoted) scan per search
issues.calibration: 500 candidates x ~1,500 average comparisons x 50 ns = ~37 ms per search against a ~30 ms search path - dominant and O(NxM); a set built at the hourly refresh removes it

issues.description: load_active_promos fetches the promo ruleset snapshot from Redis and json.loads the ~500 KB payload once per consumed event with no caching between events
issues.calibration: 0.5-2 ms Redis transfer plus 2-5 ms parse of 500 KB meets or exceeds the whole 5 ms/event budget; Medium effort for a TTL cache with invalidation on the ruleset-changed message

issues.description: convert parses the module _RATES_JSON currency table with json.loads on every call - the 150-currency table is constant after import
issues.calibration: ~50 us parse per call; pricing calls convert 3x per event (600/s) and checkout ~107/s per line item = ~35 ms/s of a core and 3% of the pricing event budget - a fixed per-item cost that adds up, and one fix helps pricing, checkout, and settlement

issues.description: rate_for scans the ~5,000-row flattened tax rule list linearly on every call to find the region and category pair - a dict keyed by (region, category) is one lookup
issues.calibration: 5,000 x 50 ns = ~250 us per call; pricing calls it per event (5% of the 5 ms budget) and checkout per line item - the multipliers live in the calling services, not in this file

issues.description: fetch_all serializes every result set with json.dumps(rows, default=str) as an eagerly evaluated logger.debug argument - the cost is paid even when DEBUG is off
issues.calibration: ~100 us per 25-row result x ~500 queries/s across all services = ~50 ms/s of a core, about 5% of a 2 ms query - and every service pays it because dbkit is shared

issues.description: log_request evaluates json.dumps(context) eagerly as the logger.debug argument for every request at the edge
issues.calibration: ~30 us x 1,200 req/s = ~36 ms/s of a core paid with DEBUG off

issues.description: check opens and json-parses the rate_rules.json tenant file from disk on every request - the ~2,000-entry rules file changes rarely
issues.calibration: ~0.2 ms file read + 1-2 ms parse per request = 15-25% of the 8 ms gateway p50 - a clear saving under 10x

issues.description: load_order_context awaits the buyer, cart, and address reads sequentially although the three queries are independent - asyncio.gather overlaps them
issues.calibration: 3 x ~2 ms serialized = ~6 ms where gather gives ~2 ms; saves ~4 ms of the 90 ms order budget

issues.description: send_order_event constructs a new httpx.AsyncClient per webhook call, paying TCP and TLS setup each time instead of reusing a module-lifetime client
issues.calibration: 10-30 ms connection setup x ~13 webhook calls/s; a shared client with a connection pool removes it

issues.description: get_product runs SELECT * on the products table, materializing all ~30 columns including the ~20 KB description_html, while the detail view reads 8 named fields
issues.calibration: ~0.5-1 ms extra row I/O and transfer on a ~2 ms query x 500 req/s = a 1.3-1.5x saving from naming the 8 columns

issues.description: find_affected_skus tests each candidate SKU with `sku in campaign_skus` where campaign_skus is a plain list of about 2,000 strings - a set makes the test O(1)
issues.calibration: ~30 candidate SKUs x ~1,000 average comparisons x 50 ns = 1.5-3 ms of the 5 ms event budget

issues.description: record sorts the whole 2,048-sample latency window on every observation to recompute the p99 - computing on snapshot removes the per-event sort
issues.calibration: ~150 us sort x 200 events/s = ~3% of a core and 3% of the 5 ms event budget

issues.description: normalize_query calls re.compile(QUERY_PATTERN) inside the function on every search query instead of compiling the module constant once
issues.calibration: CPython's re module caches compiled patterns, so the repeat compile is a ~0.4 us cache lookup - under 1% of the search path (the label-inflation probe from iteration 6)

issues.description: envelope rebuilds the constant security-header dict from the module _HEADER_PAIRS list on every response instead of hoisting the finished dict
issues.calibration: ~1 us x 1,200 responses/s = ~0.1% of a core; real but far under 1% of the path

issues.description: to_event builds the routing key with += over four bounded parts per event - a join or f-string does one allocation
issues.calibration: ~2 us per event, bounded at 4 parts = ~0.04% of the event budget

issues.description: normalize_sku rebuilds the str.maketrans translation table inside the function on every call instead of a module-level table
issues.calibration: ~1 us x ~500 calls/s across services - real, tiny

issues.description: build_values_clause concatenates the VALUES placeholder string with += per row in its loop - quadratic in rows, though callers flush at 100-row batches
issues.calibration: bounded at the documented 100-row batch this is tens of us per flush at ~2 flushes/s in pricing - the flush cadence (the multiplier) lives in services/pricing/history.py, not in this file

issues.description: render_sql re-renders the same named-parameter SQL template with re.sub on every call - callers pass identical templates, so a memoized render is one dict hit
issues.calibration: ~15 us x ~500 queries/s = ~8 ms/s of a core, under 1% of a 2 ms query

issues.description: top_sellers sorts all ~1.2M nightly payout rows to keep the top 50 - heapq.nlargest does the same with a 50-element heap
issues.calibration: the full sort costs seconds but runs once per night in the settlement batch - Low because the waste cannot add up

issues.description: render_report awaits summarize_fees three times with identical arguments for the header, body, and footer sections - the same GROUP BY query runs three times
issues.calibration: two redundant aggregate queries once per night - Low; call once and pass the summary to the three renderers

issues.description: order_status_view json.loads the ~25 KB items_json product snapshot blob to read only the item count and total - the scalar fields belong in order columns
issues.calibration: ~250 us decode + ~0.5 ms extra row I/O is 30-50% of a ~2 ms status query at 40 req/s = Medium; but items_json is written at order placement and read by the settlement export, so the fix is a schema migration with backfill and dual-write = Architectural, deriving P4

issues.description: facet_counts builds and traverses a nested facet-to-value-to-count map with chained dictionary hops per access where a flat composite key is one hop
issues.calibration: ~500 accesses x ~0.2 us extra hop = ~100 us of a ~30 ms search = ~0.3% = Low; flattening touches the response shaper and the cache serializer = Medium effort, deriving P4

issues.description: audit_context calls traceback.extract_stack on every audit record to derive the caller tag - stack walking per record where a passed-in tag works
issues.calibration: ~80 us x ~26 records/s (checkout orders + settlement batches) = ~2 ms/s of a core = Low; the caller tag is part of the audit record schema that the settlement export and operations dashboards consume, so changing it is Large, deriving P4

issues.description: dispatch awaits one webhook delivery per subscriber sequentially on the order placement path - the subscriber endpoints are independent and the per-subscriber timeout is 5 s, so the timeouts add up across the loop
issues.calibration: 5 subscribers x 20 ms healthy = 100 ms added to the 90 ms order budget; worst case 5 x 5 s timeout = 25 s on one request; gather cuts wall clock to the slowest subscriber. Unplanted; found and verified in the iteration-7 adjudication run

issues.description: set_item, remove_item, and clear_cart each run two separate execute statements - the updated_at stamp is a second round trip and pool acquisition per cart edit, with no transaction around the pair
issues.calibration: one extra 0.5-2 ms round trip per cart edit at a few dozen edits/s = 12-48 ms/s of wall clock; under 10x and per-edit fixed. Unplanted; adjudicated in iteration 7

issues.description: summary sorts every facet value list to keep the leading TOP_VALUES entries - heapq.nlargest does the top-k selection without the full sort
issues.calibration: ~100-200 us per search across the four facets, under 1% of the 30 ms search p50. Unplanted; adjudicated in iteration 7

false_positive_traps.description: semantic_rescore runs an O(candidates x embeddings) similarity double loop on the search path
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: Reachable only behind config.SEMANTIC_RESCORE, which services/catalog/config.py defaults to False; the catalog README states the beta is off outside allow-listed tenants

false_positive_traps.description: export_activity runs one actor lookup per activity row - reads as a hot N+1 handler
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: The route is never registered: routes.py and app.py do not import export.py - dead code

false_positive_traps.description: match_legacy_rows nests a full scan of current rows inside the legacy-row loop - O(n^2)
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: One-shot manual backfill for the 2.8 seller-id migration; never on the serving path

false_positive_traps.description: The address-copy loop opens a transaction and commits per row - deliberate mirror of BZ-IO-4
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: One-shot migration run manually during the 2.9 upgrade; the same pattern that is P1 in the pricing consumer is acceptable here. Sharpest hot/cold discrimination pair.

false_positive_traps.description: publish looks like one Redis send per event
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: Events buffer in a module list and flush() sends one pipelined command every PUBLISH_FLUSH_COUNT = 200 events - already batched

false_positive_traps.description: bin_weight looks like repeated pure computation per reservation
The load generator builds payloads with += in loops and constructs a new httpx.Client per simulated user
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: A load generator is cold by nature, and the per-user client deliberately prevents connection reuse from masking gateway behavior (stated in its docstring)

false_positive_traps.description: format_money_rows near-duplicates libs/commerce money formatting and builds a decimal.Context per row
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: This copy renders the nightly report only - the duplicate where one copy is cold; only the shared-lib original is hot

false_positive_traps.description: reserve_row takes one SELECT ... FOR UPDATE per reservation row - looks batchable
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: The docstring states the lock-ordering rule: single-row locks in SKU order keep the lock graph acyclic across concurrent multi-item reservations - a documented correctness trade-off

false_positive_traps.description: load_flag_file runs re.compile inside its per-key loop over ~30 flag keys
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: Called once at import time to build the module _FLAGS dict; flag() itself is a dict lookup

clean_code.note: One process-lifetime pool (POOL_MIN=5, POOL_MAX=20); connections reused
Reads with count=STREAM_READ_COUNT (100) and processes in batches
WHERE filters, a named column list, and LIMIT bound to SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE pushed into SQL
Token-validation cache with TTL and max size, dict + deque eviction
Module-level encoder instance; one encode per event
One transaction per order, executemany for line items, one commit
Server-side cursor with batched DELETE ... ANY($1) in GC_BATCH_ROWS chunks
format_cents uses a module-level Decimal quantize constant - in the same file as BZ-WORK-3, testing within-file discrimination
